title: Unsolvable: NDVI without a near-infrared band
query: Compute the mean NDVI of the attached scene.
answer:
Based on my inspection of the uploaded scene, I cannot compute the mean NDVI because the attached file contains only the red band — there is no near-infrared (NIR) band present.

**What I found in the scene (`scene_red_only.tif`):**

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Bands | 1 (band description: `red`) |
| CRS | EPSG:32616 (UTM zone 16N) |
| Size | 60 × 60 pixels |
| Data type | uint16 |
| Value range | 400 – 899 (raw reflectance DN) |
| NoData | none |

**Why NDVI can't be computed:** The Normalized Difference Vegetation Index requires two spectral bands:

```
NDVI = (NIR − Red) / (NIR + Red)
```

This scene contains only the **red** band — there is no near-infrared (NIR) band present. Without NIR reflectance, the NDVI formula cannot be evaluated. The values (400–899) are raw digital numbers, not NDVI (which would lie in [−1, 1]).

**What I can report instead** — the mean of the red band that *is* present:
- **Mean red reflectance (DN): ≈ 650.79** (min 400, max 899)

**To compute the mean NDVI, I need the NIR band** of the same scene. If you can provide the NIR band (or a multi-band scene containing both red and NIR), I can compute the NDVI and its mean immediately.
